newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Takeover talk drives up Kmart.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Takeover talk drives up Kmart.

text.p: Kmart Corp options volume surged as the stock rallied on takeover rumors, traders said Tuesday.
"The rumor on the Street is that KKR (Kolberg Kravis & Roberts) is interested in Kmart," one options trader said.
But he added that the retailer is scheduled to report third quarter earnings Wednesday, which also could account for some of the pickup in volume.
"That definitely isn't earnings," another trader said of the increased options volume.
By 1420 CST (2020 GMT), roughly 19,450 contracts changed hands, compared with an average of 1,500.
The bulk of the trading was in calls, with about 14,500 calls trading and 4,900 puts.
More than 7.8 million Kmart shares traded, making them the busiest on the New York Stock Exchange. Consolidated volume topped 12.6 million.
The stock was up 1-3/8 at 11, its session high.
Options traders said the takeover rumor was vague, with few details. Some traders doubted its validity.
Kmart officials were not available for comment and a spokesman for the buyout firm declined comment.
"I think the rumor's unfounded," one options trader said. "Kmart has a lot of debt."
He added that both retail and institutional investors were buying a lot of calls and selling a lot of puts.
"We've had a ton of people selling (long) puts," he said.
"They're just bailing out basically."
The Kmart December 10 put, which traded about 1,335 contracts, was down 7-16 at 3/8. The December 12-1/2 put traded more than 900 contracts and fell 1-1/8 to two.
The most active put was the January 10, which traded 1,945 contracts. It fell 7/16 to 1/2.
On the call side, the most active Kmart options were the December 12-1/2, which traded 3,965 contracts, and the December 10, which traded 3,880.
Those two options had eye-popping moves, with the December 12-1/2 climbing 700 percent, or 7/16, to 1/2. The December 10 surged 380 percent, going to 1-1/2 from 5/16.
The January 10 call traded 1,970 contracts and the 12-1/2 call traded more than 2,250 contracts.
"Overall it looks like bullish transactions, rolling over the Dec 10s, 12-1/2s and the puts," said Michael Schwartz, managing director at Oppenheimer & Co.
